• Radiocarbon dating estimates the age of organic material by measuring how much carbon-14 remains in it.

• After about 50,000 years, too little carbon-14 remains to measure reliably.
• The method cannot be used directly on most rocks, which do not contain carbon from once-living things.
• Chemist Willard Libby developed the method in the late 1940s.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize a limitation of radiocarbon dating that is related to the age of a sample. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.label: Radiocarbon dating, which Willard Libby developed in the late 1940s, cannot be used directly on most rocks because they do not contain carbon from once-living things.
Carbon-14 decays at a known rate, with a half-life of about 5,730 years.

Choice B is incorrect because the known decay rate is what makes the method work, not a limitation. Choice D is incorrect because it concerns the method’s history.

As a result,
Similarly,

Similarly,
Thus,
